I have helped companies with public tenders for fifteen years, and I always start with the same advice. Read the requirements first, not the price. Most proposals are rejected for very simple reasons. The company forgot a certificate, or it sent the documents one hour after the deadline. In a tender, you must follow every rule, even the small ones. If the notice says that you have to sign every page, you have to sign every page. You don't have to be the biggest company to win. But you need to be the most organized one. My tip is simple: make a checklist of every requirement, and ask a colleague to check it again before you submit.

Hi Luciana, this is Priya from the partner team in Bangalore. I have read the hospital tender, and I want to be sure that our joint bid is eligible. First, the hospital needs a letter from us, as the manufacturer. I will send it this week, so you don't have to ask for it. Second, your engineers have to show a valid certificate for our cameras. Two of the certificates on your list expired last month, so those engineers need to take the online exam again. And one more thing: the warranty must be five years, not three. We can offer that, but we need to confirm the price before Friday. Call me when you can.

When we buy technology for the hospital, the price is only one part of the decision. Our tenders have three kinds of requirements. Some are mandatory. For example, every supplier must offer support twenty-four hours a day, because a hospital never closes. Some are technical. The new cameras need to work with our current software, or we have to change the whole system. And some are only good to have. Suppliers don't have to visit the hospital before the tender, but the ones who visit usually write much better proposals. And one rule always surprises people. If you win, you mustn't change the engineers on the project without our approval.
